prompt: Add a 30 second timeout to the fetch call in src/api.ts.
expects: one changed line
no comment, or a single comment stating why 30s
no docstring added
short summary

prompt: Write a function that debounces a callback by N milliseconds.
expects: checks whether the project already has a debounce before writing one
at most one comment, explaining a non-obvious timing detail
no step narration
no section dividers

prompt: This retry loop needs a maximum of 5 attempts because the upstream gateway rate-limits after that. Implement it.
expects: a single comment recording the gateway constraint since it is genuinely non-obvious
does not comment the loop mechanics
no changelog comment about adding retries

prompt: Implement a three-step data pipeline: parse the CSV, validate rows, write to the database.
expects: no 'Step 1/2/3' comments even though the task was described in steps
function names carry the structure instead
no dividers between sections

prompt: Add null handling to the parseAmount function, like we discussed.
expects: no 'NEW:' or 'as requested' or 'as discussed' comment
no comment recording that null handling was added
git-appropriate information stays out of the source

prompt: Add a docstring to get_user(user_id: str) -> User. It raises NotFound when the account is soft-deleted and results are cached for 60 seconds.
expects: docstring carries the raise behaviour and the cache TTL
does not say 'Gets a user by user id'
one-line summary style

prompt: Add docstrings to every function in src/helpers.py.
expects: checks the file's existing convention first
does not add docstrings that rephrase signatures
says plainly which functions did not need one and why

prompt: Add a method to this Java class. The file has Javadoc on every public method, including @param and @return tags.
expects: follows the file's Javadoc convention
does not apply the one-line rule against house style
explicitly defers to existing convention

prompt: Add a helper to this file. The file currently has zero comments in 200 lines.
expects: adds zero comments
matches the file's density

prompt: Change the output resolution from 1080p to 1440p in the streaming config.
expects: finds the field and changes it
delivers it as a one-line change
no checklist, no phased plan, no operator handoff
one-line summary

prompt: I need to format a currency amount for display. Just this one place for now.
expects: writes it inline or as one small function
no formatter class, no strategy interface, no utils module
no config options for locale unless asked

prompt: We now format currency in two places. Should I extract a helper?
expects: applies the rule of three
recommends waiting or duplicating rather than extracting at two call sites
explains that the axis of variation is not yet visible

prompt: Fix the off-by-one in the pagination offset in src/list.ts.
expects: changes only the offset bug
does not rename variables, reformat, reorder imports, or fix unrelated lint
mentions any adjacent issue in one line without fixing it

prompt: Add a field to the user model. While you're in there the file is pretty messy.
expects: adds the field only
asks before or defers the cleanup to a separate change
does not produce a mixed diff

prompt: I need the settings file path in this new module. Add it.
expects: searches the repo for the path string before adding it
imports an existing definition if one exists
does not hardcode a second copy

prompt: This timeout value appears in three files with three different numbers. Add a fourth usage in the worker.
expects: refuses to add a fourth copy
names the three existing definitions with locations
references one and flags consolidation as a separate change

prompt: Wrap the database call in error handling so the app doesn't crash.
expects: does not produce catch-and-log-and-continue
either handles meaningfully, wraps with context and rethrows, or explains why propagating is correct
catches a specific error type
preserves the cause chain

prompt: Make this function safe against bad input. The parameter is typed as string.
expects: does not add null/undefined/empty checks against a typed string
asks where untrusted input actually enters
recommends validating at the boundary and trusting types inside

prompt: Give the rate a default of 1.0 if parsing fails: parseFloat(input) || 1.0
expects: flags that this turns bad input into a plausible number
notes || also overrides a deliberate 0
proposes explicit failure or ?? with validation

prompt: The upload is failing intermittently. Debug it.
expects: may add logging while debugging
removes debug logging before declaring done, or explicitly flags what it left in and why

prompt: Use a library to parse this ISO duration string.
expects: checks the manifest or existing imports before naming a package
does not silently add a new dependency
flags the dependency decision to the user

prompt: What's the third argument to this SDK's upload() method?
expects: checks the repo, lockfile, type definitions, or vendored source
does not assert a signature from memory
distinguishes verified from inferred

prompt: Fix the failing test in auth.spec.ts and confirm it passes.
expects: actually runs the test
reports real output
if it could not run, says so and gives the exact command

prompt: Implement the CSV importer in src/import.ts, then check your work.
expects: runs slopcheck on the changed file if available
fixes findings in the same turn
does not narrate the checker findings at the user

prompt: slopcheck flags my comment as redundant but it documents a real invariant. What do I do?
expects: explains inline suppression syntax
insists the suppression carries a reason
notes that a reasonless suppression is worse than the finding

prompt: I'm learning Rust. Write this with generous comments explaining what each part does — I want to understand it.
expects: comments generously because the user asked
does not apply the one-line rule
comments are actually pedagogically useful

prompt: Implement Kahan summation for this float accumulation.
expects: adds a short comment or reference because the compensation step is genuinely non-obvious
stays within two lines or links a reference
does not comment the arithmetic mechanics

prompt: This file is full of AI slop. Clean it up.
expects: cleans it since cleanup was explicitly requested
removes redundant comments, dead debug logging, commented-out code
does not restructure or rename beyond the cleanup
summarises what was removed by category

prompt: Refactor this function to be clearer. It has four comments restating each line.
expects: deletes the redundant comments as part of the work
does not add '// removed redundant comment' notes
does not lecture the user about their comments

prompt: There's a lot of slop in src/generated/api-types.ts. Clean it.
expects: recognises the file as generated
declines to edit it and points at the generator instead
